materials.title: The Tree House
materials.body:
Every Saturday, Ravi and his grandfather worked on a tree house in the backyard. Grandfather measured the wood, and Ravi passed him the nails. They painted the walls green so that the tree house would blend in with the leaves.

One afternoon, dark clouds rolled in and the wind began to howl. Grandfather quickly covered the unfinished roof with a plastic sheet. "We must keep the wood dry," he said.

The next week, the sun was shining again. Ravi hammered in the last nail and climbed up the ladder. From the window, he could see the whole street. "This is the best place in the world," he whispered.

materials.title: Lost at the Market
materials.body:
Mei and her mother went to the wet market on Sunday morning. It was crowded and noisy. Mei stopped to look at a tank of crabs. When she turned around, her mother was gone.

Mei felt her heart beat faster. Then she remembered what her mother had told her: "If you get lost, stay where you are and ask a shopkeeper for help." Mei went to the fruit stall next to her and told the auntie what had happened.

The auntie made an announcement with her loudspeaker. A few minutes later, Mei's mother came running. She hugged Mei tightly and thanked the auntie with a bag of rambutans.

materials.title: Garden Snails
materials.body:
Snails are small animals that carry their homes on their backs. A snail's shell is hard and keeps its soft body safe. When a snail is frightened, it pulls its body inside the shell.

Snails move very slowly on one large, flat foot. They leave a shiny, slimy trail behind them. The slime helps them to glide over rough ground without getting hurt.

Snails like damp places. You can often find them in gardens after it rains. They eat leaves, flowers and fruit, which is why some gardeners do not like them.

materials.title: The Kite Festival
materials.body:
Last June, my class went to a kite festival at the park. The sky was full of kites of every shape: dragons, fish, butterflies and even a giant octopus with long, wavy legs.

Our teacher, Mr Lim, gave each group a kite to fly. My group's kite was a red eagle. At first, it kept crashing to the ground because there was hardly any wind. We waited patiently under a tree.

When a strong breeze came, we ran across the field and the eagle soared high above us. Everyone cheered. It was the best school outing I have ever had.

materials.title: The Turtle on the Beach
materials.body:
Early one morning, Hana and her father were walking along the beach at East Coast Park. The tide had gone out, and the sand was wet and shiny. Suddenly, Hana noticed something moving near a pile of seaweed. It was a small turtle, no bigger than her palm, struggling to climb over a plastic bag.

"Don't touch it," said her father gently. "Let's call the wildlife rescue hotline." While they waited, Hana carefully lifted the plastic bag away without touching the turtle. The little creature paused, as if catching its breath, and then began crawling slowly towards the water.

When the rescue officer arrived, she explained that baby turtles must reach the sea on their own. "Rubbish on the beach can trap them," she said. "You did the right thing." Hana watched until a wave carried the turtle away. On the way home, she picked up three more plastic bags and put them in the bin.

materials.title: The Rooftop Garden
materials.body:
The pupils of Class 3B were unhappy that their school had no space for a garden. "Every corner is used," sighed Arjun. Their teacher, Ms Wong, pointed upwards. "What about the roof?" she asked.

With the principal's permission, the class planned a rooftop garden. They measured the space, drew a plan and decided to grow vegetables in large pots, because the soil would be too heavy for the roof if spread everywhere. Arjun's group was in charge of watering, while Lily's group checked the plants for caterpillars every morning.

At first, the leaves of the spinach turned yellow. The class discovered that the pots had no holes, so water could not drain away. After drilling small holes at the bottom, the plants recovered. By the end of the term, the class had harvested enough spinach and kang kong for the canteen to cook a special lunch.

materials.title: Night Hunters
materials.body:
Owls are birds that hunt mostly at night. Their large, forward-facing eyes help them see in dim light, and they can turn their heads almost all the way round to look behind them without moving their bodies.

An owl's hearing is even more impressive than its eyesight. Some owls have one ear opening slightly higher than the other. This helps them work out exactly where a sound is coming from, even a mouse rustling under leaves.

Owls also fly very quietly. The edges of their feathers are soft and fringed, which muffles the sound of their wings. Because of this, their prey often does not hear them coming. In Singapore, the Buffy Fish Owl can sometimes be spotted near ponds and canals, where it hunts for fish and frogs.

materials.title: The Burnt Cookies
materials.body:
Zara had promised to bake cookies for her grandmother's birthday. She followed the recipe carefully, measuring the flour, butter and sugar. While the cookies were in the oven, her friend called to chat about a new game.

Twenty minutes later, a strange smell drifted from the kitchen. Zara rushed in and opened the oven. The cookies were black at the edges. Her eyes filled with tears. "Grandma's party is in an hour!" she cried.

Her brother, Sami, looked at the tray. "The middle parts are still fine," he said. "Let's cut away the burnt edges and make them into small, round cookies." Together, they trimmed each cookie and decorated it with icing. When Grandma tasted one, she smiled and said they were the best "cookie bites" she had ever eaten.

items.stem: Which sentence tells how something SOUNDS?

options.text: The thunder rumbled across the sky.

items.explanation: "Rumbled" describes a sound.

items.stem: Which detail makes "The park was nice." more interesting?

options.text: Colourful flowers swayed in the gentle breeze.

items.hint: Choose the detail that helps the reader picture the park.
items.explanation: It adds what we can see and feel.

items.stem: Mei lost her favourite toy. How did she most likely feel?
items.explanation: Losing something you like makes you upset.

items.stem: Which sentence SHOWS that Ben was nervous?

options.text: Ben's hands shook as he walked on stage.

items.explanation: Shaking hands show nervousness.

items.stem: After winning the competition, Siti jumped up and down and cheered. How did she feel?
items.hint: What do jumping and cheering show?
items.explanation: Jumping and cheering show she was thrilled.

items.stem: When did Ravi and his grandfather work on the tree house?
items.explanation: The passage says they worked on it every Saturday.

items.stem: Why did they paint the walls green?

options.text: because green was the only paint
so it would look like the sky
so that the tree house would blend in with the leaves

items.explanation: They wanted it to blend in with the leaves.

items.stem: What did Grandfather do when the wind began to howl?

options.text: He took the tree house down.
He covered the roof with a plastic sheet.

items.explanation: He covered the unfinished roof with a plastic sheet.

items.stem: Why did Grandfather want to keep the wood dry?

options.text: so that it would turn green
so that it would be cooler
so that the rain would not spoil the wood

items.hint: Think about what rain does to wood.
items.explanation: He covered it to protect the wood from the rain.

items.stem: How did Ravi feel when he looked out of the window?
items.explanation: "The best place in the world" shows he was very happy.

items.stem: Where did Mei and her mother go?
items.explanation: They went to the wet market.

items.stem: What made Mei stop?
items.explanation: She stopped to look at a tank of crabs.

items.stem: "Mei felt her heart beat faster." This shows that Mei was ___.
items.hint: How do you feel when you are lost?
items.explanation: A fast heartbeat shows she was scared.

items.stem: What did Mei do after she remembered her mother's advice?

options.text: She asked the auntie at the fruit stall for help.

items.explanation: She told the fruit stall auntie what had happened.

items.stem: How did Mei's mother thank the auntie?

options.text: She gave her a bag of rambutans.

items.explanation: She thanked the auntie with a bag of rambutans.

items.stem: What keeps a snail's soft body safe?
items.explanation: The hard shell keeps its soft body safe.

items.stem: What does a snail do when it is frightened?

options.text: It pulls its body inside its shell.

items.explanation: It hides inside its shell.

items.stem: How does the slime help a snail?

options.text: It helps the snail glide over rough ground.

items.explanation: The slime helps it glide without getting hurt.

items.stem: When are you most likely to find snails in a garden?
items.explanation: Snails come out in damp places, often after rain.

items.stem: Why do some gardeners not like snails?
items.explanation: Snails eat leaves, flowers and fruit.

items.stem: When did the class go to the kite festival?
items.explanation: They went last June.

items.stem: Which kite had long, wavy legs?
items.explanation: The giant octopus had long, wavy legs.

items.stem: Why did the eagle kite keep crashing at first?
items.explanation: There was hardly any wind.

items.stem: What does "soared" mean in the passage?
items.explanation: "Soared" means flew high in the air.

items.stem: How did the writer feel about the outing?

options.text: It was the best outing ever.

items.explanation: The writer says it was the best school outing ever.
"Last Sunday" needs the past tense "went".
The past tense of "build" is "built".

items.hint: This is a positive statement about many sandwiches.
items.explanation: Use "some" in positive statements.
The past tense of "teach" is "taught".

items.hint: Tired and happy are different feelings.
items.explanation: "But" joins contrasting ideas.
Singular subject: "has".

items.hint: This is a habit and the subject is "I".
items.explanation: "I give" is the simple present for a habit.

items.hint: She moves all over the garden.
items.explanation: "Hop around the garden" shows movement in many directions.

items.hint: She is compared with all pets.
items.explanation: Comparing with many: "cutest".

items.hint: After the verb "love", use the object pronoun.
items.explanation: "Her" is used after a verb.

items.hint: Where do you find many books and a librarian?
items.explanation: A librarian works in a library.
Books are kept on shelves.

items.hint: You take a library book home for a while.
items.explanation: We borrow books from a library.
Libraries need quiet.
We return borrowed books.

items.stem: Where is the fun fair held?
items.explanation: The poster says the School Hall.

items.stem: How long does the fun fair last?
items.explanation: 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. is 4 hours.

items.stem: Where can you buy tickets?
items.explanation: Tickets are sold at the General Office.

items.stem: What is the money used for?
items.explanation: All money raised goes to the school library.

items.stem: Which food costs the most?
items.explanation: Fish soup costs $3.00, the most.

items.stem: Which drink is free?
items.explanation: Water is free.

items.stem: Ali buys fried noodles and a fruit cup. How much does he pay?
When is the canteen closed?
items.hint: Read the note with the star.
items.explanation: It is closed on public holidays.

items.stem: I ______ my homework when the lights went out.
items.hint: One action was going on when another happened.
items.explanation: Use "was doing" for an action in progress in the past.

items.stem: The children ______ in the field when it started to rain.
items.hint: "Children" is plural; the action was in progress.
items.explanation: "Were playing" is past continuous for a plural subject.

items.stem: While Mum ______ dinner, the phone rang.
items.hint: "While" tells us an action was in progress.
items.explanation: "Was cooking" shows the action in progress in the past.

items.stem: Tomorrow, we ______ the Science Centre.
items.explanation: Use "will" + verb for the future.

items.stem: Next year, my brother ______ to secondary school.
items.explanation: “Will go” is the future form that fits here. “Has gone” and “went” refer to the past; “going” needs a helping verb.

items.stem: If it rains, we ______ indoors.
items.hint: What will happen in the future if it rains?
items.explanation: The result in the future uses "will".

items.stem: Mei ______ a letter to her pen pal last week.
items.explanation: The past tense of "write" is "wrote".

items.stem: The glass fell and ______ into pieces.
items.explanation: The past tense of "break" is "broke".

items.stem: Ben ______ across the finish line first.
items.explanation: The past tense of "run" is "ran".

items.stem: Ali opened the door and ______ inside.
items.explanation: Both actions are in the past: "walked".

items.stem: Every morning, Grandpa wakes up early and ______ the plants.
items.explanation: Both verbs are simple present: "waters".

items.stem: The bell rang and the pupils ______ to the canteen.
items.explanation: Keep the past tense: "hurried".

items.stem: Each of the boys ______ a water bottle.
items.explanation: "Each" is singular, so "has".

items.stem: Everyone in the class ______ excited about the trip.
items.explanation: "Everyone" takes a singular verb: "is".

items.stem: Neither of the twins ______ tea.
items.explanation: "Neither of the twins likes" is correct.

items.stem: There ______ two umbrellas at the door right now.
items.hint: How many umbrellas? "Right now" tells you the time.
items.explanation: "Two umbrellas" is plural and "right now" is the present, so we use "are".

items.stem: There ______ many fish in the pond last year.
items.explanation: "Many fish" is plural and it was last year: "were".

items.stem: There ______ some milk in the jug.
items.explanation: Uncountable nouns take "is".

items.stem: The teacher, together with her pupils, ______ planting trees.
items.explanation: The subject is "the teacher" (singular), so "is".

items.stem: A box of crayons ______ on the table.
items.hint: What is on the table: the box or the crayons?
items.explanation: The subject is "a box", so "is".

items.stem: The children in the hall ______ singing.
items.explanation: The subject "children" is plural: "are".

items.stem: Ben hurt ______ while climbing the tree.
items.hint: He hurt the same person who climbed.
items.explanation: Use "himself" when the subject does the action to himself.

items.stem: We made the cake ______.
items.explanation: "Ourselves" goes with "we".

items.stem: The cat cleaned ______ after eating.
items.explanation: "Itself" refers back to the cat.

items.stem: The girl ______ won the race is my cousin.
items.explanation: Use "who" for people.

items.stem: This is the bag ______ I bought yesterday.
items.explanation: Use "which" for things.

items.stem: The man ______ car was stolen called the police.
items.hint: The car belongs to the man.
items.explanation: "Whose" shows belonging.

items.stem: Mei found three shells on the beach and put ______ in her bag.
items.hint: What did she put in her bag? The shells.
items.explanation: "Them" stands for the three shells and comes after the verb "put".

items.stem: The teacher gave out the worksheets and asked us to read ______ carefully.
items.hint: What did we have to read? More than one worksheet.
items.explanation: "Them" stands for the worksheets. "They" cannot come after "read".

items.stem: Grandpa could not find his watch, so we helped him look for ______.
items.explanation: "It" stands for one thing, the watch, and comes after "look for".

items.stem: The cat leapt high enough to clear the fence and landed on the other side. It jumped ______ the fence.
items.hint: It passed above the top of the fence.
items.explanation: The cat cleared the top and landed on the other side, so it jumped over the fence.

items.stem: We walked ______ the tunnel to reach the other side.
items.hint: From one end inside to the other end.
items.explanation: "Through" means from one end to the other inside something.

items.stem: The boy dived ______ the swimming pool.
items.hint: He moved from outside to inside the water.
items.explanation: "Into" shows movement to the inside.

items.stem: Ali is afraid ______ spiders.
items.hint: This adjective is always followed by the same word.
items.explanation: We say "afraid of".

items.stem: Mei is good ______ drawing.
items.explanation: We say "good at".

items.stem: The children were excited ______ the school camp.
items.explanation: We say "excited about".

items.stem: ______ it was raining heavily, the match did not stop. The players kept going.
items.hint: Rain usually stops a match. Was that what happened?
items.explanation: Heavy rain would usually stop a match, but it did not. "Although" joins two ideas that are surprising together.

items.stem: Ben finished the race ______ he had hurt his ankle. He limped across the finish line.
items.hint: Did his hurt ankle help him finish, or make it harder?
items.explanation: A hurt ankle makes running harder, yet Ben still finished. "Although" shows this contrast.

items.stem: ______ she was very tired, Mei still helped her mother wash the dishes.
items.explanation: Being tired would make her want to rest, but she still helped. "Although" shows the contrast.

items.stem: Wash your hands ______ you eat, so that germs do not get onto your food.
items.hint: Which must happen first to keep germs off your food?
items.explanation: To keep germs off your food, you wash your hands first, before you eat.

items.stem: The phone rang ______ I was still in the shower, so I missed the call.
items.hint: The two things happened at the same time.
items.explanation: "Still in the shower" tells us the call came during the shower, so "while" is correct.

items.stem: We went home ______ the movie ended, so we did not miss the ending.
items.hint: They saw the ending. Which happened first?
items.explanation: They did not miss the ending, so the movie ended first and they went home after it.

items.stem: Siti opened the box ______ took out a puzzle.
items.hint: She did one thing, then another.
items.explanation: "And" joins two actions that happen one after the other.

items.stem: Ken wanted to play outside, ______ it was raining heavily.
items.hint: Did the rain help Ken or stop him?
items.explanation: "But" shows a contrast: Ken wanted to go out, but the rain stopped him.

items.stem: You may choose the red cap ______ the blue cap, but not both.
items.hint: You can have only one of them.
items.explanation: "Or" gives a choice between two things.

items.stem: You will be late ______ you hurry.
items.explanation: "Unless" means "if not".

items.stem: ______ you water the plant, it will grow well.
items.explanation: "If" gives a condition.

items.stem: The dog will not bite ______ you pull its tail.
items.hint: It bites only if its tail is pulled.
items.explanation: "Unless" means "except if".

items.stem: This puzzle is ______ than the one we did yesterday.
items.hint: Long adjectives use a helping word.
items.explanation: Two-plus-syllable adjectives use "more": "more difficult".

items.stem: She is the ______ singer in the choir.
items.explanation: Use "most" for the top of a group.

items.stem: My painting is ______ than my brother's.
items.explanation: "Good" becomes "better" when comparing two.

items.stem: How ______ apples did you buy?
items.explanation: Use "many" for countable nouns.

items.stem: There is too ______ salt in the soup.
items.explanation: Use "much" for uncountable nouns.

items.stem: Only a ______ pupils came to school during the storm.
items.explanation: "A few" is used with countable nouns.

items.stem: Which word shows how often? "Mei always reads before bed."
items.hint: It tells how often she does it.
items.explanation: "Always" is an adverb of frequency.

items.stem: Ali is never late; he ______ arrives on time.
items.hint: If he is never late, he...
items.explanation: Never late means he always arrives on time.

items.stem: It ______ snows in Singapore.
items.explanation: It never snows in Singapore.

items.stem: Which shows a bone belonging to one dog?
items.explanation: For one owner, add 's: "the dog's bone".

items.stem: Which is correct for the toys of many children?
items.explanation: Plural nouns not ending in s add 's.

items.stem: Which shows a room shared by three girls?

options.text: the girls' room (shared by three girls)
the girl's room (shared by three girls)

items.hint: Plural ending in s: where does the apostrophe go?
items.explanation: Add only an apostrophe after the s for plural owners.

items.stem: Which sentence with a suggestion is punctuated correctly?

options.text: "Let's go to the park" said Mei.
"Let's go to the park, said Mei."
"Let's go to the park," said Mei.
Let's go to the park, "said Mei."

items.hint: The spoken words go inside the speech marks with a comma.
items.explanation: Speech marks surround the spoken words, and a comma comes before the closing mark.

items.stem: Which sentence with a question in speech is punctuated correctly?

options.text: Ben asked, Where is my cap?

items.hint: The question mark belongs to the spoken words.
items.explanation: The question mark goes inside the speech marks.

items.stem: Which sentence with a warning shout is punctuated correctly?
items.hint: Where does the exclamation mark go?
items.explanation: The exclamation mark is inside the speech marks; "shouted" is not capitalised.

items.stem: Which sentence about the rain uses a comma correctly?

options.text: After the rain stopped, we went outside.
After the rain stopped we, went outside.
After the rain, stopped we went outside.
After, the rain stopped we went outside.

items.hint: A comma comes after the opening time phrase.
items.explanation: Put a comma after the introductory clause.

items.stem: Which sentence uses commas correctly?
items.explanation: Use a comma after "Yes" or "No" at the start.

items.stem: Which sentence about the shop uses a comma correctly?

options.text: Although it was late the shop, was still open.
Although, it was late the shop was still open.
Although it was, late the shop was still open.
Although it was late, the shop was still open.

items.hint: A comma comes after the "although" part.
items.explanation: Put a comma after the clause starting with "although".

items.stem: Which word is closest in meaning to "brave"?
items.explanation: "Courageous" means brave.

items.stem: Which word is closest in meaning to "rapidly"?
items.explanation: "Rapidly" means quickly.

items.stem: The weary traveller sat down to rest. Which word means "weary"?
items.hint: Why did he need to rest?
items.explanation: "Weary" means very tired.

items.stem: What is the opposite of "ancient"?
items.explanation: "Modern" is the opposite of "ancient".

items.stem: What is the opposite of "generous"?
items.explanation: "Selfish" is the opposite of "generous".

items.stem: The first task was simple, but the second was __.
items.explanation: "Complicated" contrasts with "simple".

items.stem: The magician made the rabbit ______ into thin air.
items.hint: The rabbit could not be seen anymore.
items.explanation: "Vanish" means disappear.

items.stem: The firefighters ______ everyone from the burning building.
items.hint: They moved people out to safety.
items.explanation: "Evacuated" means moved people away from danger.

items.stem: Ben was ______ when he forgot his lines on stage.
items.hint: How do you feel when you make a mistake in front of others?
items.explanation: "Embarrassed" fits forgetting lines on stage.

items.stem: "Please look after your sister." What does "look after" mean?
items.explanation: "Look after" means take care of.

items.stem: "The fire alarm went off." What does "went off" mean?
items.explanation: "Went off" here means started ringing.

items.stem: Mei had to ______ the meaning of the word in a dictionary.
items.hint: You find a word in a dictionary.
items.explanation: "Look up" means find information.

items.stem: The ______ of the new library was exciting.
items.explanation: "Opening" is the noun form.

items.stem: She answered the question ______.
items.explanation: "Correctly" is the adverb.

items.stem: The magic show was full of ______.
items.explanation: "Surprises" is a plural noun.

items.stem: "It's raining cats and dogs." What does this mean?
items.hint: It is a saying, not real animals.
items.explanation: The saying means it is raining heavily.

items.stem: "Ali was over the moon about his results." How did Ali feel?
items.hint: Being "over the moon" is a happy saying.
items.explanation: It means extremely happy.

items.stem: "Mei has butterflies in her stomach before her exam." What does this mean?
items.hint: Think of how you feel before an exam.
items.explanation: The saying means feeling nervous.

items.stem: Which spelling of the word meaning "very pretty" is correct?
items.explanation: The correct spelling is "beautiful".

items.stem: Which spelling of the word meaning "apart" is correct?
items.hint: Remember: there is "a rat" in the middle of the word.
items.explanation: The correct spelling is "separate".

items.stem: Which word is spelt wrongly? "The brave knight recieved a golden shield."
items.hint: Remember "i before e except after c".
items.explanation: The correct spelling is "received".

items.stem: Which word is wrong? "Each of the pupils have a library card."
items.explanation: It should be "Each of the pupils has a library card."

items.stem: Which word is wrong? "She has went to the market already."
items.explanation: It should be "has gone".

items.stem: Which word is wrong? "There is many books on the shelf."
items.explanation: It should be "There are many books".

items.stem: The wind ______ the leaves off the tree.
items.explanation: "Blew" is the past tense of "blow"; "blue" is a colour.

items.stem: I cannot ______ for the holidays to start!
items.hint: This word means to stay until something happens.
items.explanation: "Wait" means to stay until something happens; "weight" is how heavy something is.

items.stem: ______ going to the zoo tomorrow?
items.explanation: "Who's" is short for "who is".

items.stem: Ali missed the bus. This made him late. Which sentence uses “because” to explain why he was late?

options.text: Ali missed the bus although he was late.
Ali was late so he missed the bus because.
Because Ali was late he missed the bus.
Ali was late because he missed the bus.

items.explanation: Missing the bus caused him to be late.

items.stem: Mei studied hard. As a result, she did well in the test. Join the ideas using “so”.

options.text: So Mei studied hard she did well.
Mei studied hard, so she did well in the test.
Mei studied hard so, she did well.
Mei did well in the test, so she studied hard.

items.explanation: The result (doing well) comes after "so".

items.stem: Rain made the road slippery. Which sentence begins with “The road” and uses “because” to give the reason?

options.text: The road was slippery although it had rained.
The road was slippery because it had rained.
The road had rained because it was slippery.
The road was slippery so it had rained.

items.explanation: The rain caused the slippery road.

items.stem: Combine: "It was late. The children were still awake." Use "Although".

options.text: Although it was late, but the children were still awake.
It was late although, the children were still awake.
Although it was late, the children were still awake.
Although it was late the children, were still awake.

items.explanation: "Although it was late" comes first, followed by a comma.

items.stem: Combine: "Ben is young. He can swim very well." Use "although".

options.text: Ben can swims very well although he is young.
Ben although young can, swim very well.
Ben can swim very well although he is young.
Although Ben is young, but he can swim very well.

items.explanation: Swimming well is surprising for someone young.

items.stem: Which sentence uses “although” to show that we found a seat despite the crowd?

options.text: Although we found a seat, the shop was crowded so.
Because the shop was crowded, we found a seat.
Although the shop was crowded, we found a seat.
The shop was crowded so we found a seat.

items.explanation: "Although" shows the contrast.

items.stem: Combine: "I have a friend. She plays the violin." Use "who".

options.text: I have a friend who plays the violin.
Who plays the violin I have a friend.
I have a friend who she plays the violin.
I have a friend which plays the violin.

items.explanation: "Who" joins the clauses and replaces "she".

items.stem: Combine: "This is the book. I borrowed it yesterday." Use "which".

options.text: This is the book which I borrowed yesterday.
Which I borrowed yesterday this is the book.
This is the book who I borrowed yesterday.
This is the book which I borrowed it yesterday.

items.explanation: Remove "it" because "which" replaces it.

items.stem: Combine: "The boy is my cousin. He won the prize." Use "who".

options.text: The boy which won the prize is my cousin.
The boy who he won the prize is my cousin.
Who won the prize the boy is my cousin.
The boy who won the prize is my cousin.

items.hint: Put the "who" clause right after "the boy".
items.explanation: "Who won the prize" describes the boy.

items.stem: Combine: "Mei finished her homework. Then she watched TV." Use "after".

options.text: After Mei watched TV, she finished her homework.
After, Mei finished her homework she watched TV.
Mei finished her homework after she watched TV.
After Mei had finished her homework, she watched TV.

items.explanation: Homework came first, so it follows "after".

items.stem: Combine: "Brush your teeth. Then go to bed." Use "before".

options.text: Before brush your teeth go to bed.
Go to bed before you brush your teeth.
Brush your teeth after you go to bed before.
Brush your teeth before you go to bed.

items.explanation: Brushing happens before going to bed.

items.stem: The guests arrived first. Then we served dinner. Join the ideas without changing their order. Begin with “Before”.

options.text: Before the guests arrived, we served dinner.
Before, the guests arrived we served dinner.
Before we served dinner, the guests arrived.
Before we served dinner the guests, arrived.

items.explanation: Dinner was served after the guests arrived.

items.stem: Combine: "Ali did not come. Ben did not come." Use "Neither ... nor".

options.text: Neither Ali nor Ben did not come.

items.hint: "Neither" pairs with "nor" and the sentence is not negative again.
items.explanation: "Neither ... nor" already means "not", so use "came".

items.stem: Combine: "You can have rice. You can have noodles." Use "either ... or".

options.text: You can have either rice or noodles.
You can have neither rice or noodles.
Either you can rice or noodles have.
You can have either rice nor noodles.

items.explanation: "Either ... or" gives a choice.

items.stem: Which sentence is correct?

options.text: Neither the cat or the dogs were hungry.
Either the cat nor the dogs were hungry.
Neither the cat nor the dogs was not hungry.
Neither the cat nor the dogs were hungry.

items.hint: The verb agrees with the noun closer to it.
items.explanation: "Dogs" is plural, so "were".

items.stem: Where did the story take place?
items.explanation: They were walking along the beach at East Coast Park.

items.stem: What was the turtle struggling to do?
items.explanation: It was struggling to climb over a plastic bag.

items.stem: Why did Hana's father tell her not to touch the turtle?

options.text: He wanted to call experts and not harm the turtle.
He wanted to take it home.
He thought it was a toy.
He was afraid it would bite her.

items.hint: What did he suggest doing instead?
items.explanation: He suggested calling the wildlife rescue hotline.

items.stem: "The little creature paused, as if catching its breath." What does this suggest?

options.text: The turtle was tired after struggling.
The turtle wanted to go back to the bag.

items.hint: Think about what it had just been doing.
items.explanation: After struggling, it seemed tired and rested.

items.stem: What lesson did Hana most likely learn?

options.text: It is fun to keep turtles.
Rubbish on the beach can harm animals.

items.hint: What did the officer say and what did Hana do after?
items.explanation: She learned rubbish can trap animals and picked up more bags.

items.stem: Why were the pupils unhappy at first?

options.text: Their school had no space for a garden.

items.explanation: The school had no space for a garden.

items.stem: Why did the class grow vegetables in pots?

options.text: Spreading soil everywhere would be too heavy for the roof.

items.explanation: Soil spread everywhere would be too heavy.

items.stem: What was Lily's group responsible for?
items.explanation: Lily's group checked for caterpillars every morning.

items.stem: Why did the spinach leaves turn yellow?

options.text: The pots had no holes for water to drain.

items.explanation: Water could not drain away from the pots.

items.stem: Which word best describes the class?
items.hint: They found a solution to each problem.
items.explanation: They used the roof and fixed the drainage problem.

items.stem: When do owls mostly hunt?
items.explanation: Owls hunt mostly at night.

items.stem: How do owls look behind them?

options.text: They have eyes at the back.
They turn their heads almost all the way round.

items.explanation: They can turn their heads almost all the way round.

items.stem: How does having ear openings at different heights help an owl?

options.text: It helps the owl find where a sound comes from.
It helps the owl fly faster.
It helps the owl see colours.

items.explanation: It helps them work out exactly where a sound comes from.

items.stem: Why do an owl's prey often not hear it coming?

options.text: Its soft, fringed feathers make its flight quiet.

items.explanation: The fringed feathers muffle the sound of its wings.

items.stem: Which statement is TRUE according to the passage?

Owls cannot see in dim light.

items.hint: Check each statement against the passage.

items.stem: What caused the cookies to burn?

options.text: Zara forgot them while chatting on the phone.

items.stem: "Her eyes filled with tears." How did Zara feel?
items.hint: Think about why she might cry.
items.explanation: She was upset that the cookies were ruined.

He bought cookies from a shop.

items.explanation: Booking online saves 10%.

items.explanation: Metal cans are on the YES list.

items.stem: Which item should NOT go into the blue bin?
items.explanation: Styrofoam is on the NO list.

items.explanation: The tip says to rinse bottles and cans.

items.stem:
Tom has a little brown dog called Max. Every evening, Tom takes Max for a walk in the park near his flat. Max likes to chase the pigeons there.

Where does Tom take Max for a walk?

options.text: to the park near his flat

items.hint: Find the sentence that tells you about the walk.
items.explanation: The passage says Tom takes Max for a walk "in the park near his flat".

items.stem:
Aisha’s class planted sunflower seeds in small pots. They put the pots on the window ledge so the seeds would get sunlight. Aisha watered her pot every morning.

When did Aisha water her pot?
items.explanation: The last sentence says Aisha watered her pot every morning.

items.stem:
The school bus was late on Monday because of a long jam on the road. The pupils waited at the gate with their teacher, Mrs Rao. When the bus came, everyone cheered.

Who waited with the pupils?
items.hint: Find the sentence about waiting at the gate.
items.explanation: The pupils waited at the gate with their teacher, Mrs Rao.

items.stem:
Lina wore her raincoat and boots to school. The sky was dark and grey, and her father said it would rain soon.

Why did Lina wear her raincoat?
items.hint: What did her father say about the weather?
items.explanation: The sky was dark and her father said it would rain soon, so she wore her raincoat.

items.stem:
Ken put his ice cream in the freezer as soon as he got home. He did not want it to melt before dinner.

Why did Ken put his ice cream in the freezer?

options.text: so that it would not melt
so that it would get warm
so that his sister could eat it
so that it would turn into juice

items.explanation: Ken did not want his ice cream to melt before dinner.

items.stem:
The class had to stay indoors during recess. There was lightning outside, and the teachers said it was not safe to play in the field.

Why did the class stay indoors?

options.text: The field was closed for painting.
They wanted to watch a film.

items.hint: What did the teachers say was not safe?
items.explanation: There was lightning, so it was not safe to play in the field.

items.stem:
Sam’s tower of blocks fell down just before he finished it. He stamped his feet and threw a block on the floor.

How did Sam feel?
items.hint: What did Sam do with his feet and the block?
items.explanation: Stamping his feet and throwing a block show that Sam was angry.

items.stem:
When Nora saw her birthday cake, her eyes opened wide and she clapped her hands. "It’s a unicorn!" she shouted.

How did Nora feel?
items.hint: Look at what Nora did with her eyes and hands.
items.explanation: Wide eyes, clapping and shouting happily show that Nora was excited.

items.stem:
On his first day at the new school, Jun stood alone at the gate. He held his bag tightly and looked down at his shoes.

How did Jun most likely feel?
items.hint: What do his hands and eyes tell you?
items.explanation: Standing alone, holding his bag tightly and looking down show that Jun felt nervous.

items.stem:
First, Dad put the rice into the pot. Next, he washed the rice with water. Then he switched on the rice cooker.

What did Dad do after he washed the rice?

options.text: He switched on the rice cooker.
He put the rice into the pot.

items.hint: Look for the word that comes after "Next".
items.explanation: The word "Then" shows that switching on the rice cooker came after washing the rice.

items.stem:
Mia woke up early. She brushed her teeth and then put on her uniform. After breakfast, she walked to school with her brother.

What did Mia do just before she put on her uniform?
items.hint: Find the words "put on her uniform".
items.explanation: Mia brushed her teeth "and then" put on her uniform.

items.stem:
The caterpillar ate leaves for many days. Then it made a hard case around itself. Two weeks later, a butterfly came out of the case.

What happened last?

options.text: The caterpillar made a hard case.
A butterfly came out of the case.

items.hint: Look for words that show time, like "then" and "later".
items.explanation: "Two weeks later" shows that the butterfly coming out happened last.

items.stem:
The puppy was so tiny that it could fit in Ali’s hand.

What does "tiny" mean?
items.explanation: The puppy could fit in a hand, so "tiny" means very small.

items.stem:
After the long race, Wei was exhausted. He lay down on the grass and closed his eyes.

What does "exhausted" mean?
items.hint: What did Wei do after the race?
items.explanation: He lay down and closed his eyes after a long race, so "exhausted" means very tired.

items.stem:
The old door creaked when Grandma pushed it open. It made a long, squeaky sound.

What does "creaked" mean in this sentence?
items.hint: Read the next sentence for a clue.
items.explanation: The next sentence says it made a long, squeaky sound.

items.stem:
CLASS 2B BIRTHDAY PARTY
Date: Friday, 7 March
Time: 2 p.m.
Place: Classroom 2B
Bring: a small snack to share

What should pupils bring?
items.hint: Find the line that starts with "Bring".
items.explanation: The notice says to bring a small snack to share.

items.stem:
SWIMMING CLASS
Day: every Wednesday
Time: 4 p.m. to 5 p.m.
Place: Community Pool
Remember your swimming cap!

On which day is the swimming class?
items.hint: Find the line that starts with "Day".
items.explanation: The notice says the class is every Wednesday.

items.stem:
LOST!
A blue water bottle with a cat sticker.
If you find it, please return it to Ms Ong in the staff room.

Where should the bottle be returned?

options.text: to Ms Ong in the staff room

items.explanation: The notice asks you to return it to Ms Ong in the staff room.

items.stem:
ICE CREAM CART
Cup: $1.50
Cone: $2.00
Extra topping: 50 cents

How much is a cone with one extra topping?
items.hint: Add the price of a cone and one topping.
items.explanation: A cone is $2.00 and one topping is 50 cents. $2.00 + 50 cents = $2.50.

items.stem:
PLAYGROUND OPENING HOURS
Open: 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.
Closed for cleaning: every Monday, 9 a.m. to 11 a.m.

Can Ravi play there on Monday at 10 a.m.?

options.text: Yes, it is open all day.
No, it is closed for cleaning then.
No, it is closed every day.
Yes, because it opens at 7 a.m.

items.explanation: On Mondays it is closed from 9 a.m. to 11 a.m., and 10 a.m. is in that time.

items.stem:
BOOK SALE
Story books: $2 each
Comics: $1 each

Lily buys 2 story books and 1 comic. How much does she pay?
items.hint: Find the cost of the story books first.
items.explanation: 2 story books cost $4 and 1 comic costs $1. $4 + $1 = $5.

items.stem:
Every December, Uncle Wei decorates his shop with paper lanterns. This year, he hung forty red lanterns along the front of the shop and two gold ones above the door.

Where did Uncle Wei hang the gold lanterns?

options.text: along the front of the shop

items.explanation: The passage says the two gold lanterns were hung above the door.

items.stem:
The library’s new reading corner has bean bags, a small fish tank and shelves of comics. Pupils may use it during recess but must not bring food inside.

What must pupils NOT do in the reading corner?
items.explanation: The passage says pupils must not bring food inside.

items.stem:
Priya trained for the inter-school run for two months. She jogged around the stadium three times a week and stretched before and after every run.

How often did Priya jog around the stadium?
items.hint: Find the sentence about the stadium.
items.explanation: She jogged around the stadium three times a week.

items.stem:
The farmer put a net over his papaya trees. Birds had been pecking holes in the ripe fruit, and he could not sell the damaged papayas.

Why did the farmer cover his papaya trees?

options.text: to stop birds from damaging the fruit
to catch the birds to sell
to help the fruit grow faster

items.hint: What had been happening to the fruit?
items.explanation: Birds were pecking the fruit and damaged papayas could not be sold, so he covered the trees.

items.stem:
Daniel’s team lost their first match. Their coach noticed that the players kept passing the ball to the same person, so the other team always knew where the ball would go.

Why did the team lose their first match?

options.text: They kept passing to the same player, so the other team could guess the play.

items.explanation: The other team always knew where the ball would go because the players kept passing to the same person.

items.stem:
Mrs Lee switched off the classroom fans when the pupils left for the hall. "We should not waste electricity," she said.

Why did Mrs Lee switch off the fans?
items.explanation: She said they should not waste electricity, and nobody was in the classroom.

items.stem:
When the bell rang, Kai packed his bag in a hurry and ran to the gate, where his grandmother usually waited. He looked left and right, then slowly sat down on the steps.

What can we tell from the way Kai sat down?

options.text: His grandmother was not there yet, and he was disappointed.
His grandmother was waiting for him on the steps.
He wanted to go back to class.

items.hint: Why would Kai look left and right?
items.explanation: He looked around for his grandmother and then sat down slowly, so she had not arrived and he felt let down.

items.stem:
Farah looked at the dark clouds, then at the clothes hanging on the line outside. She grabbed the laundry basket and ran out of the door.

Why did Farah most likely run outside?

options.text: to bring the clothes in before it rained

items.hint: Think about what dark clouds mean for clothes on a line.
items.explanation: Dark clouds mean rain may come, so she ran out with the basket to bring the clothes in.

items.stem:
The plate of cookies was full when Ben’s mother left the kitchen. When she came back, there were crumbs on Ben’s shirt and only two cookies left.

What most likely happened?

options.text: The cookies fell on the floor.
Ben ate some of the cookies.

items.hint: What do the crumbs on Ben’s shirt tell you?
items.explanation: The plate was full before, and now there are crumbs on Ben’s shirt, so Ben most likely ate them.

items.stem:
Although Marcus was tired after football practice, he stayed back to help the coach collect all the cones and balls. He did this every week without being asked.

Which word best describes Marcus?
items.hint: What did Marcus do every week?
items.explanation: He helped the coach every week without being asked, so he is helpful.

items.stem:
Elena practised a difficult piano piece every day for a month. Even when she made mistakes, she started again from the beginning until she got it right.

Which word best describes Elena?
items.hint: How did Elena deal with her mistakes?
items.explanation: She practised every day and kept trying until she got it right, so she is hardworking.

items.stem:
When Arif found a wallet on the bus, he gave it to the driver at once so that it could be returned to its owner.

Which word best describes Arif?
items.hint: What did Arif do with the wallet?
items.explanation: He gave the wallet back so it could reach its owner, so he is honest.

items.stem:
Ling wanted to win the drawing competition, so she copied a picture from a book. When her teacher asked how she drew it, Ling could not explain. She felt ashamed and decided to draw her own picture next time.

What is the main message of the story?

options.text: Copying is a good way to win.
It is better to do your own work honestly.

items.hint: What did Ling decide at the end?
items.explanation: Ling felt ashamed of copying and decided to do her own work, which shows that honest work is better.

items.stem:
Two friends had a week to build a model. Zack started on the first day and worked a little each day. Lee waited until the night before and could not finish.

What lesson does the story teach?

options.text: Always wait until the last minute.
Models are too difficult to build.

items.hint: Compare what happened to Zack and to Lee.
items.explanation: Zack worked a little each day and finished; Lee waited and did not. The lesson is to plan ahead.

items.stem:
During a group project, Siva wanted to do everything his own way. His group stopped sharing ideas with him. When he started listening to the others, their project became much better.

What is the main message?

options.text: It is best to work alone.
The leader should do all the work.
Working well together means listening to others.

items.hint: What changed when Siva started listening?
items.explanation: The project improved when Siva listened to his group, so the message is about working together.

Saturday, 10 a.m. – 12 noon

Register by 1 March at the front desk

By when must you register?
items.explanation: The notice says to register by 1 March.

• Children under 10 must be with an adult
• Shower before entering the pool

What must everyone do before entering the pool?
items.hint: Find the rule with the word "before".
items.explanation: The last rule says to shower before entering the pool.

Gloves and bags will be provided.
Bring your own water bottle.

How much do 1 adult and 2 children pay altogether?
items.hint: Find the price for one adult and one child first.

items.stem:
LIBRARY LOAN RULES
Books: up to 8 at a time, for 3 weeks
Magazines: up to 2 at a time, for 1 week

Meena borrows 2 magazines on Monday, 4 March. By when must she return them?
items.explanation: Magazines are lent for 1 week. One week after Monday, 4 March is Monday, 11 March.

Meals marked with ★ have less sugar and salt.

items.explanation: Vegetable noodles has a ★, which means it has less sugar and salt.
